hero.title: Put AI into the job an industry actually does
hero.description: Ruyin turns digital-twin situation, LLM assessment, and multi-agent execution into a reusable foundation, then reassembles it around how each industry really works. Every industry solution starts from one real scenario: data it can ingest, a workflow it can survive, an outcome it can explain — and grows from there.
hero.patternAlt: Abstract geometric wireframe sphere, standing for many industries converging on one foundation

lowAltitude.name: Low-altitude Economy
lowAltitude.summary: One dispatch foundation for airspace, routes, and flight missions
lowAltitude.title: Getting drones airborne is the easy half
lowAltitude.description: Drone and eVTOL density is rising fast, and the bottleneck is not the aircraft — it is how airspace gets carved up, how routes get sequenced, and what happens when something goes wrong. The solution puts airspace resources, flight plans, live tracks, and ground support on one twin, and hands the repetitive dispatch and compliance calls to agents.

capabilities.title: Airspace and route twin
capabilities.description: Controlled airspace, no-fly zones, buildings, weather, and ground crowds become a computable 3D base map that route planning solves directly against.

capabilities.title: Flight mission orchestration
capabilities.description: Application, approval, release, and recovery run online; conflict detection and slot allocation are automatic, and people only handle exceptions.

capabilities.title: Surveillance and response
capabilities.description: Live tracks are matched against filed routes, so deviation, loss of link, and no-fly incursion alert instantly with an actionable next step.

scenarios: Batch scheduling and conflict resolution for urban delivery corridors
Inspection mission dispatch across power lines, pipelines, and waterways
Temporary airspace control for large events and incidents
Operational oversight and data collection for low-altitude service stations

emergency.name: Emergency Management
emergency.summary: A closed loop from early warning to post-incident review
emergency.title: From seeing an incident to organising a response
emergency.description: The hard part of emergency command was never getting the data — it is forming one judgement out of fragments fast enough, then landing the order on a person. A digital twin carries the situation, an LLM produces the assessment and the shared wording, and agents track teams, supplies, notifications, and acknowledgements so every response compounds into the next one.

capabilities.title: Digital-twin situation base
capabilities.description: Cities, parks, basins, roads, and risk sources mapped one-to-one, supporting incident location, impact analysis, and resource reachability.

capabilities.title: LLM assessment core
capabilities.description: Automatic multi-source briefing, plan and precedent retrieval, and traceable reasoning behind every recommended action.

capabilities.title: Multi-agent execution
capabilities.description: Monitoring, assessment, dispatch, notification, public sentiment, and review each own a lane and keep pushing the incident forward.

scenarios: Extreme weather and urban flooding: inundation modelling and evacuation
Hazardous materials and industrial park incidents: impact-radius assessment
Forest and urban firefighting: spread modelling and force deployment
Large events: crowd, security, and medical coverage monitoring

energy.name: Energy & Power
energy.summary: Operational assessment and maintenance coordination for the new power system
energy.title: The more renewables you connect, the faster you have to decide
energy.description: Distributed PV, storage, and flexible load multiply uncertainty, and both dispatch and maintenance now have to make more calls in less time. Asset registers, telemetry, weather forecasts, and outage plans sit on one simulatable model, and the repetitive analysis, sequencing, and reporting goes to agents.

capabilities.title: Whole-system situation
capabilities.description: Plants, lines, storage, and distributed generation modelled together, with output, load, and section margin visible and replayable.

capabilities.title: Forecasting and simulation
capabilities.description: Output and load forecasts from weather and historical curves, plus consequence modelling for maintenance, faults, and extreme weather.

capabilities.title: Maintenance agents
capabilities.description: Defect detection, work-order dispatch, spare-part allocation, and restoration tracking chained together, with field and control room on the same progress.

scenarios: Renewable output forecasting and deviation assessment
Distribution fault location, isolation, and restoration planning
Automatic defect detection and maintenance scheduling
Peak summer and winter load and resource balancing

industrial.name: Industrial Operations
industrial.summary: Turning shop-floor expertise into callable agent capability
industrial.title: The veteran engineer’s judgement should be callable
industrial.description: On a plant floor the most expensive asset is rarely the equipment — it is the judgement held by a handful of people. Process parameters, asset registers, inspection records, and work instructions become a searchable knowledge base, and agents take over the high-frequency calls: scheduling, quality attribution, fault diagnosis, and operator guidance.

capabilities.title: Process and asset knowledge base
capabilities.description: Procedures, drawings, parameters, histories, and past work orders structured together, with every answer traceable to its source.

capabilities.title: Quality and anomaly attribution
capabilities.description: Inspection results linked to parameters, batches, shifts, and equipment state, producing a verifiable attribution path rather than a correlation guess.

capabilities.title: Scheduling and shop-floor coordination
capabilities.description: Orders, capacity, materials, and staffing solved together; changes trigger a re-plan and push actionable instructions to the shift.

scenarios: Fast attribution and process traceback for batch quality drift
Diagnostic suggestions and maintenance knowledge for equipment anomalies
Onboarding guidance and procedure Q&A for new operators

ecosystem.title: More industries, built together
ecosystem.description: Four industries are only the start. What actually makes AI work inside an industry is the people who know it — integrators, design institutes, equipment makers, vertical software vendors, consultancies. Ruyin opens up the foundation, model access, agent orchestration, and operations layer; the domain knowledge and the customer relationship stay with the partner. We only take the hard, generic engineering underneath.

partners.title: Solution partners
partners.description: Bring the domain know-how, package your own industry solution on the platform, and deliver it independently.

partners.title: Technology and integration partners
partners.description: Existing systems, algorithms, or hardware plug into the orchestration and operations layer through open interfaces.

partners.title: Channel and advisory partners
partners.description: Teams who know the regional market and the customer process, working end to end from scenario discovery to rollout.

contact.title: Talk to the ecosystem team
contact.description: Tell us your industry, the scenario in front of you, and the kind of partnership you have in mind. We will put the right solution and engineering people on it, starting from one scenario we can prove.
contact.note: Still exploring? That is fine — you do not need a finished scenario to start the conversation.

hero.title: Digital Twin Agentic Solution for Emergency Management
hero.description: Build a live digital twin for regions, cities, parks, and critical sites, then layer LLM-based assessment and multi-agent execution across monitoring, decision support, plan simulation, resource dispatch, field coordination, and post-incident review.
hero.imageAlt: Emergency command and dispatch visualization screen

intelligence.title: From seeing an event to organizing a response
items: Sensor, video, IoT, and business data are registered in one twin base to form a live operating picture.
The LLM turns fragmented event information into risk summaries, response suggestions, and command wording.
Agents keep tracking teams, supplies, notices, tasks, and review actions so instructions become execution.

architecture.title: Three-layer capability architecture
architecture.description: This is not just a command screen. It separates situation awareness, model reasoning, and execution coordination into deployable layers that can grow from one pilot scenario to a city-scale emergency system.

items.title: Digital twin situation base
items.description: Map cities, parks, watersheds, roads, critical facilities, and risk sources into a virtual-real model for event localization, impact analysis, and resource reachability.
points: Unified spatial map and risk objects
Live overlay of events, teams, supplies, and facilities
Simulation for flooding, fire, congestion, evacuation, and more

items.title: LLM assessment center
items.description: Support natural-language queries, event summaries, plan retrieval, risk explanation, and communication drafting for command teams.
points: Retrieval of plans and historical cases
Traceable assessment evidence and action suggestions

items.title: Multi-agent execution
items.description: Divide monitoring, assessment, dispatch, notification, public communication, and review into cooperating agents that keep advancing the event workflow.
points: Status tracking for teams, vehicles, supplies, and arrival
Incident timeline, outcome review, and optimization suggestions

flow.title: Cover the full emergency response lifecycle
flow.description: Create a loop across pre-event warning, in-event command, and post-event review, turning every response into better capability for the next one.

steps.title: Risk monitoring
steps.description: Connect weather, water, fire, traffic, video, and IoT data to detect and locate abnormal events earlier.

steps.title: Situation twin
steps.description: Overlay people, facilities, risk sources, shelters, warehouses, and event progress on one twin map.

steps.title: Intelligent assessment
steps.description: Read structured and unstructured information to generate incident level, impact area, secondary risks, and response priorities.

steps.title: Plan simulation
steps.description: Compare response plans and dispatch strategies against event level, roads, resources, weather, and safety constraints.

steps.title: Command coordination
steps.description: Agents track tasks, teams, supplies, notifications, and acknowledgements to keep the command center synchronized.

steps.title: Review optimization
steps.description: Compile timelines, bottlenecks, resource consumption, and outcome reviews to improve plans and the knowledge base.

agents.title: Agent matrix for emergency management
agents.description: Each agent owns a clear emergency task domain and collaborates through shared situation, shared knowledge, and shared task state.

items.title: Monitoring and warning agent
items.description: Analyzes indicators, thresholds, video clues, and public reports to identify anomalies and trigger graded warnings.

items.title: Situation briefing agent
items.description: Turns event progress, department feedback, field photos, and historical records into readable command briefings.

items.title: Plan simulation agent
items.description: Retrieves plans based on event type and constraints, then creates response paths and risk notes.

items.title: Resource dispatch agent
items.description: Matches teams, vehicles, supplies, equipment, and experts, calculates arrival time, and tracks allocation status.

items.title: Field coordination agent
items.description: Pushes tasks, routes, safety notes, and acknowledgement requirements to field teams with less manual relay.

items.title: Review assessment agent
items.description: Generates review reports, key timelines, response metrics, and plan revision suggestions.

scenarios.title: Start with four emergency scenarios
scenarios.description: Begin with frequent, high-impact scenarios that clearly require cross-agency coordination, then turn them into demonstrable and repeatable industry templates.

items.title: Extreme weather and urban flooding
items.description: Combine rainfall, water levels, roads, pump stations, and shelters to simulate flooding, detours, and relocation strategies.

items.title: Hazardous chemicals and industrial parks
items.description: Assess impact areas and response boundaries using enterprise data, hazard sources, wind direction, population, and fire resources.

items.title: Forest and urban fire coordination
items.description: Fuse fire points, wind field, combustible materials, fire stations, and water sources to support spread simulation and force deployment.

items.title: Large events and public safety
items.description: Monitor crowds, traffic, security positions, and medical support to detect congestion and conflict risks earlier.
